result.answer: Under the PFAS NEMP 3.0 drinking-water values, PFOS on its own is 0.07 ug/L, and this matches the value for PFOS and PFHxS added together [G1]. Under the current ADWG drinking-water values, PFOS is 0.008 ug/L, and PFOS and PFHxS are checked separately rather than as a sum [G2]. The ADWG fact sheet says PFOS in drinking water should not go above this health-based level [2].

result.answer:
There are seven categories: report not substantiated, possibly contaminated (investigation required), not contaminated (unrestricted use), contaminated (restricted use), remediated for restricted use, contaminated (remediation required), and decontaminated [1].

A site is put in the report not substantiated category when a report gives no real grounds to suspect contamination [1][8].

Some categories lead to a memorial on the certificate of title, which alerts owners and planning authorities to known or suspected contamination [4][5].

result.answer: A sampling and analysis quality plan (SAQP) is a plan that makes sure the data collected is representative, giving a solid basis for decisions [1]. In Western Australia, it should be prepared before any samples are taken, and it should fill critical gaps in the conceptual site model (CSM) [2]. It should link each area of concern to the sampling planned there and be included in the site assessment report [2][3].
